newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB Report-Indicator price up A$5.00 a tonne.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB Report-Indicator price up A$5.00 a tonne.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) multigrade indicator price rose A$5.00 a tonne to A$131.75 delivered Newcastle over the past week, AWB said in its weekly grain market report.
The impact of weather damage had begun to show in some harvest samples, AWB said. Northern parts of South Australia should begin harvesting this week, it said.
The milling wheat market came to life in Queensland last week with cash prices rising by between A$15.00 and A$18.00 a tonne for premium grades.
Even feed grain prices firmed slightly, the AWB said.
The trend was not repeated in other states and canola prices conrtinued to weaken during the week to A$352.00 a tonne delivered Melbourne, the AWB said.
On international developments, AWB said the EU Commissiion dropped its wheat subsidies by about A$10 a tonne in the past week with French wheat now priced at A$183 a tonne.
Argentine wheat prices also firmed with deliveries for January, February and March now offered at A$167 a tonne.
Taiwan bought U.S. wheat during the past week at A$265 a tonne for high protein dark northern spring and A$206 a tonne for western white wheat, it said.
